context:
Goal: the lane lint's findings are caught before a push leaves.
Problem (risk): the guard cannot read a commit that has not landed yet, so #2077 refuses any commit, merge, pull or rebase in the same call as `git push`, with "run the push in a call of its own". Claude often writes `git commit -m x && git push`, so each such push costs one retry in every repo with a fast lint step.
Based on (code): hooks/guard_merge.py lane_lint_push_hit, chain branch, on #2077.
Based on (read): main refuses a chained push today only when the commit follows a step the guard cannot read and conflict markers may be in play (conflict_markers_hit, merged 2026-11-07); a plain `git commit -m x && git push` passes on main.
Based on (review): round 3 (reviewer sonnet) passed with positive net safety value; the retry rate is unmeasured.
Departs from: main, where a plain commit-then-push in one call passes — adds a refusal of every commit-making step before a push in one call.
Meanwhile: the lane goes on with the refusal kept (records, lane lint, hand-off). Your answer can change it later.

options.gain: No chained push sends commits past the lane lint.
options.how: #2077 merges as it is: a push runs in a call of its own after the commit lands.
options.label: Keep the refusal
options.lose: One retry for each chained push, in every repo with a fast lint step.

options.how: #2077 lets a chained push through with a note that it could not lint, and lints nothing for it.
options.label: Allow the chain
options.lose: A chained push, the way Claude pushes most often, sends commits the lane lint never read.

ref: PR #2077 (refuse a push whose commits fail the lane lint's fast checks); debt lane-lint-chain-blanket-deny
reply: Withdrawn by triage, 10:51 CST Nov 8: the pick can be undone before #2077 merges, so it is the lane's call (item 423 ruling). The lane keeps the refusal (option a); debt lane-lint-chain-blanket-deny tracks the retry cost.
short: Lane-lint push: refuse commit + push in one call?
title: May the lane-lint push check refuse a commit and a push in one call?
